Subscribe to the channel for more videos like this in the future and let's dive into it. Back in late January of this year we spoke about how these historical crossovers between the bull market EMAs, the green 21 week and the purple 50 week eMA, once those crossovers occur they're not really kind to Bitcoin's price action. But that's not just been the case dating back to 2018 it's also been the case dating to 2014 so we saw a few cycles worth of that data take place here and of course by late or at least early February of this year, we already saw price action drop to 60k once we got that crossover take place, very similar to the downside that we saw across cycle to cycle. So where does that leave us now? Because we've seen the crossover take place in this cycle. We've seen the downside also in this cycle, we've also seen the downside materialise post crossover. So what goes on next and looking back across time, once those crossovers happen we do see periods of relief. Sometimes very brief periods and sometimes really extended periods and in 2022 we actually saw that period of clustering last a few good months before we capitulated into that final bear market bottoming out formation whereas in 2018 we saw the major wave of capitulation right into the cluster of price action that represented the bear market bottoming out formation, and 2014 showed us also something differently. Because we saw the crossover take place, we saw clustering in the price action occur beneath these bull market Mas, before ultimately distributing and ending up with additional capitulation into a really extended bear market bottling out formation. We can see that each crossover event leads to a bear market bottom over time, but it does take time. It does take a substantial amount of time to see that bear market bottling out formation develop. The bear market capitulation final bottom also takes time in and of itself. And the way that this capitulation takes place, well, it differs from cycle to cycle, but the takeaway is still the same, that it does take time. We do see periods of relief and clusters in the meantime. And so, if we're indeed now slowly starting to uptrend and uptick a little bit, then obviously being six months into this bear market and historically we tend to see the bear market lasts anything from a year to just over a year so just doing this we can come up with a rough approximation and you can see here from 2014 that this bear market bottom took a few weeks beyond the 1-year mark. So this would be half way, then, you know. This is half way roughly or maybe even slightly higher. We still had a decent amount of downside and a decent amount of time wasted in this cycle as well. So it's not just in terms of the downside and it's not in terms of just time, but it's also the downside. That's my point here. And halfway through the bear market, we were still clustering around this level for quite a while before dissipating to new lows and 2014, quite similar, by the midpoint we were still meandering and zigzagging Before additional downsides took place here So what we're seeing from all these cycles really is that once the crossover takes place We do see additional downside also take place over time whether that happens rapidly whether that takes a bit more time whether we see a bit more clustering in terms of relief before that downside takes place it really does take time and so when people say to me that I've been talking about really low plat prices for for bitcoin's price action and we're not quite seeing that just yet i think we have to broaden our time horizon because uh every bear market lasts roughly a year and we're only six months in so i wouldn't imagine that we're going to go to really low prices tomorrow or even after tomorrow even a week from now two two weeks from now, we have an entire six-month period to still see that additional downside. formation so we had the relief periods a little bit earlier on in that cycle and these relief periods took place prior to the crossover itself so that's that's also a slight difference whereas here
